Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well. We’re ramping a new internal product that will increase our Redwood usage by ~30% starting in April. Our current contract with Redwood runs through 2026-12-31 with committed capacity and an annual seat allotment. Can you share pricing options for: 
- a mid-contract increase (pro-rated add-on vs uplift pricing)
- the option to co-term the expanded capacity now and move to a single renewal date (we prefer a 12-month term)
- any incentives or discounts for expanding above 25% mid-term

Attached is a short procurement summary of our internal approval flow. Also include PO/billing steps and any lead times for onboarding additional capacity.

Subject: Re: Request: adding capacity mid-contract + co-term options

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the procurement note. A few quick clarifying Qs before I build formal options: 
1) Is the 30% increase expected to be sustained for the remainder of the current term or a temporary burst (e.g., 2–3 months)?
2) Are you expecting to increase committed spend (reserved capacity) or just need short-term burst/GPU capacity?

High level we typically offer three paths:
- Option A: Pro-rated add-on at list rates (fastest; no changes to renewal).
- Option B: Co-term now + expansion credit (we roll the added capacity into a new 12-mo term with an expansion discount).
- Option C: Short-term burst + evaluation credits (if you want to trial higher throughput before committing).

I’ll put together a quote showing costs and effective unit pricing for each option — looping Marissa on pricing guidance and Evelyn for billing/PO flow. If you’re free I can do a quick 20-min call this afternoon to walk through.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: pricing guidance for BrightOak expansion

Karthik / Evelyn — quick internal note on numbers I’d be comfortable proposing given BrightOak’s account size and renewal behavior: 

Assumptions: current ARR bucket = $250k, planned expansion ~30% (~$75k incremental if fully committed). Renewal due 2026-12-31.

Recommended public options to present:
- Pro-rate add-on (Option A): list rate for added capacity, no discount. Good for small/short bursts.
- Co-term + Expansion Discount (Option B): move to a new 12-mo term now; apply a 12% expansion discount on incremental capacity and 5% on base for the remaining old term to incentivize co-term. (Requires finance sign-off for anything above 15% total effective discount.)
- Enterprise Addendum (Option C): if they commit to a larger reserved capacity (>=50% increase), offer a stepped discount up to 18% and 30-day SLA uplift. Needs RevOps approval.

Notes: don’t offer >18% off-list without manager approval. If they ask for credit for historical usage we can provide a one-time uplift credit up to 5% applied on the first invoice.

I’ll approve up to 12% on expansion for you; any steeper ask ping me and I’ll escalate to Markus.

-Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Summary (two options):
Option 1 — Fast Add-on (no co-term)- Immediate add of 30% capacity at list rates; pro-rated for the remainder of the current term.- No change to renewal date.- Typical lead time: 48–72 hours to provision.

Option 2 — Co-term + Expansion Discount (recommended if expansion is sustained)- Combine current + incremental into a new 12-mo term starting now.- Expansion discount: 12% on incremental capacity; 5% credit applied to base for overlapping period.- Requires a signed amendment and PO.- Lead time: 3–5 business days for finance/contract review.

Also available: short-term burst nodes for very high throughput months (priced separately).

Next steps I propose: 1) Confirm whether expansion is sustained; 2) If co-term desired I’ll send an amendment + DocuSign link; 3) If PO route, Evelyn will confirm invoicing details.
